cells.tense: The sensing and the adjusting are working together in this moment, and you are the one holding both.
cells.ask: Pick one exchange you've been keeping level. Say out loud what you gave and what came back, then let it stand without squaring it up.
cells.core:
You notice when something tilts, and you've started bringing it back before anyone asks. It happens in small movements — a little more given here, a little less taken there — and most days nobody sees the adjusting. Steady, not stiff. The balance isn't a spot you landed on. It's one you keep making.

Keeping it takes ongoing correction, not standing still. One exchange in front of you stays even mostly because you've been quietly working at it, and a word about that would fit — not a correction, a mention that the work is real. Naming it doesn't tip the scale. The thing you're holding level stays level, and the other person gets to see what keeps it there.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel a tilt and you're already steadying it.
cells.verb: feeling your way to what's fair
cells.place: at the point where balance is kept by continuous adjustment

cells.tense: You're ahead of a reckoning that hasn't arrived, tallying what things will cost before they land.
cells.ask: Name one place you're running a tally. Write down the part that's actually yours, do only that part today, and leave the ledger closed till next week.
cells.core:
You're several steps ahead of what's here, working out how things will balance before they've happened. There's a future version where it all comes out even, and you're rehearsing for it — which turns ordinary exchanges into tabs, and gestures into entries that have to be repaid. The accounting is eating the ease it was meant to guard.

Nothing is wrong with the instinct. It's doing sums when it could be doing contact. What's shared with you doesn't have to come out even right away. It has to have you in it. The reckoning you're bracing for hasn't landed, and no amount of pre-counting makes it come fairer. Put the pen down and let the give and take run for a while.

cells.tense: You're standing at a threshold where the plain word would have opened the room, and the word doesn't come.
cells.ask: Choose one small, low-stakes thing you've been letting slide. Tell the person it involves, in one plain sentence, no explanation attached.
cells.core:
What's fair still registers in you, and it isn't reaching anyone. Saying a wrong out loud made the room worse, so you stopped saying it — and the quiet worked well enough to become the habit. The sense of it is intact. The speaking of it isn't.

The step from sensing to acting has gone missing, and one small true thing, spoken plainly, does more than a dozen swallowed ones. You've been keeping things smooth by keeping them unsaid, and the smoothness is thinner than it looks. The exercise isn't to win anything. Say it simply to one person, and let the reply be whatever it is.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair. You've stopped saying it.

cells.tense: The adjusting is happening — you are the one doing it — and you'd call it simply being fair-minded.
cells.ask: Say 'I noticed' once today, out loud, to someone you've been quietly keeping things even for.
cells.core:
You sense a tilt and you move toward it before it becomes a problem — the extra given, the unevenness quietly corrected, the room kept right without a word. You'd explain it as having a decent character, not as a skill in use. The skill is in use. The credit for it hasn't landed anywhere.

Under that is a direct read on what's fair that doesn't need argument. It arrives. You trust it enough to act on it, and you file it under the situation's demands or the other person's need or simply how things are. It's you, keeping the balance. Saying you noticed doesn't make you important. It just puts your name on something you keep doing.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping things fair. You call it being decent.
